comment: Attributes one side's emitted document states and the other's omits, where BC's own reader produces the SAME object either way (#4357). These are NOT declared differences: on every entry here the two derivations agree, and what is declared is that the agreement carries no information. tests/expectations/metadata-equivalence/allowlist.json is the other file and means the opposite — a tolerated DISAGREEMENT. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over the Business Foundation and System Application bundles, 1,286 objects; docs/metadata-equivalence.md#unobservable-omissions has the table and the method. The original 18 entries were triaged on #4400; every entry records a verdict — should-state, legitimately-less, or needs-a-named-measurement — and cites the OPEN issue that owns the work rather than the triage issue itself. An undeclared omission fails the run, and an entry matching nothing fails it too unless it is versionContingent — which here means 'fewer than 10 of the 1,286 objects carry it on the measured build', a population one BC version's object churn can remove.

omissions.reason: TRIAGED (#4400): the runner SHOULD state it — derivable from data the symbol file already carries, and the omission is a gap. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): BC states it on 558/558 codeunits, 'StaticAutomatic' 555 and 'Manual' 3; SymbolReference.json declares an EventSubscriberInstance property on exactly 3, all 'Manual', so 'declared value, else StaticAutomatic' reproduces BC on 558 of 558 with no residue. Cost: one field on CodeunitMetaRow plus one SetAttribute in TryBuildCodeunitMetadataEquivalenceXml. NOT AL-observable — CodeUnit Metadata (2000000137) declares no such column (its 11 fields are read from the platform package's own CodeUnitMetadata.Table.al), so this is document-equivalence only. Tracked on #4605 (re-homed from #3788, which closed with the codeunit method table).

TRIAGED (#4400): the runner SHOULD state it, and it is the cheapest of the 18 — a constant. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): BC writes MetadataVersion='130000' on 558/558 codeunits, one value, no variation, and the same 130000 appears as a <MetadataVersion> element on every XmlPort and Report document. It is a property of the document FORMAT, not of any declaration, which is why it is uniform. #4279 already states the consequence for a different member: every BC reader copies this attribute into MetaXxx.MetadataToken, so the runner stating nothing leaves BC's default of 0 and MetadataToken differs on every object of several kinds. That makes this one omission the cause of allowlisted DIFFERENCES elsewhere, which is why it is tracked there rather than treated as cosmetic.

TRIAGED (#4400), then CORRECTED by #4442: saying less is CORRECT here, and the triage verdict above it ("the runner SHOULD state it") was wrong. The triage measured the DOCUMENT and inferred the column; a real service tier had already measured the column and disagreed. Corpus PR 296 asked eight cloud legs what CodeUnit Metadata's RequiredTestIsolation reports for a TestRunner declaring TestIsolation = Disabled: every leg answered None, and those assertions were withdrawn rather than adjusted. Mechanism, re-derived from the binary on #4442: MetaCodeunit's ctor matches the attribute name 'RequiredTestIsolation' (21 chars, read out of its PropertyRequiredTestIsolation constant in Microsoft.Dynamics.Nav.Types.dll 28.1.49838.53910) while the AL compiler emits 'TestIsolation' (13), so the parse never fires and the field keeps its ctor default None. So BC's own reader ALSO discards this attribute, which is exactly why the member-for-member comparison agrees and why the omission is unobservable rather than a gap. Corpus PR 394 pins the column at None so the suite states the measured answer instead of remembering it from a PR that deleted its own tests. Tracked by #3562, the conversion chain this document-level omission belongs to; there is no runner work owed.

TRIAGED (#4400): the runner SHOULD state it — a direct read, the simplest of the 18. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): BC states @Access on 69 of 144 enum documents, Public 54 and Internal 15, and SymbolReference.json declares an Access property on exactly those 69 with exactly those values, 69 of 69 exact. NOT AL-observable: there is no enum metadata virtual table in the platform package at all (Table Metadata has an Access column; enums have no counterpart), so this is document-equivalence only. Tracked on #4279, the open issue for the enum and permission-set derivations' residue.

A PAIRING artifact, not a derivation difference. The runner writes Enabled='true' on every subpage part, as BC does (#4282, docs/dependency-page-properties.md#part-controls), but it flattens every part into one ContentArea container while BC keeps each where the AL declared it -- inside groups, and FactBox parts in their own FactBoxArea container. This comparison pairs /Content/Containers[0]/Controls[i] by POSITION, so on a page whose first container starts with field controls the runner's i-th part is paired with BC's i-th FIELD, which states no Enabled. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910: 6 occurrences, exactly the pages 1927, 1992 (x2), 4326, 4336 and 9983, each a runner part against a BC ControlDefinition. It disappears when the runner reconstructs the control tree, which is the page-property work tracked on #4282.

TRIAGED (#4400): SAYING LESS IS LEGITIMATE TODAY, as a bounded scope decision rather than a limit — the runner reconstructs only part of the page control tree, so it states nothing on controls it does not build. docs/metadata-equivalence.md#the-control-tree-is-a-cost-decision-not-an-unprovable-one settles the direction: no page entry claims a value is underivable, and the control tree is cost and scope 'with a proof path'. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): on the depth-1 controls BC emits, every @MultiLine occurrence in THIS declaration is the value BC's reader produces when the attribute is absent and the symbol file is silent, while every symbol-stated value is a non-default the ordinary value comparison already reports. So the fix here is not a derivation but 'build more of the control tree, then write the default' — which is why it is tracked on #4282 with the rest of the page-property work rather than filed as its own gap.

TRIAGED (#4400): the runner SHOULD state it, and this is the cheapest row in the file after MetadataVersion. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): BC writes <ID Name='...'>9001</ID>, and the @Name it carries equals the <Name> element the same document states immediately below it on 4 of 4 xmlports — a duplicate of a value the runner ALREADY derives and already writes elsewhere in the same document, not a new lookup. Tracked on #3797. Kept versionContingent: 4 of 1,286 objects, and the whole population is System Application's 4 xmlports.

TRIAGED (#4400): CANNOT DECIDE WITHOUT A MEASUREMENT THIS BUNDLE CANNOT PROVIDE, and the measurement is named rather than guessed. Re-derived on BC 28.1.49838.53910, both ground-truth bundles (1,286 objects): the entire population is one occurrence on one object — Report 9810, the ONLY report in either bundle — where BC writes PromotedActionCategoriesML='' on the request page's <Properties>. Its symbol record states a RequestPage with an EMPTY Properties array, so nothing distinguishes 'BC emits empty-string for every report request page' from 'BC emits it only when something about this report is true'. One object cannot separate those, and the second is what decides whether omitting is wrong. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: ground-truth bundles for an app with several reports — Base Application has hundreds — asking whether the attribute appears on all request pages or a subset. Until then this stays declared rather than fixed, because a writer-side change would go harness-green either way, which is the exact blindness #4357 added this third state to expose. Tracked on #4282 as the page-properties issue the request page's <Properties> element belongs to. Kept versionContingent: 1 occurrence, and a bundle with no reports removes the population entirely.

TRIAGED (#4467, which added the xmlport RequestPage subtree to what this harness measures by pointing the metadata-equivalence projection at the runner's real derivation). THE UNOBSERVABILITY IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, and that is the part to check before trusting any of the 12 xmlport RequestPage entries: MetadataDocumentPresenceDiff strips the attribute from BC's OWN document, re-parses the stripped document with BC's OWN reader, and records the omission only when MetadataObjectDiff finds the two parsed objects identical. So BC's reader is what adjudicates each of these, not a claim about which attributes a master-page template supplies. THE WALK DISCRIMINATES: BC states 37 distinct Element.Attribute pairs in that subtree across System Application's 4 xmlports on 28.1.49838.53910, and it reported 12 -- Containers.ContainerType, Controls.ID, Controls.FilterTableID, Properties.PageType, Properties.Editable, the four Sorting.* attributes and 16 others were seen and NOT reported, because stripping them changes the parsed object. A run where all 37 came back would mean the probe had stopped discriminating. WHY THE RUNNER OMITS THEM (the cause, which the measurement above does not establish and does not need to): WriteXmlPortRequestPageXml derives only the FRAME, because MetadataProvider merges it into BC's own master-page template at load, so the built-in controls come from that template; what the runner does derive is the per-tableelement filter control and its expression, keyed to this xmlport's node sequence, which the template cannot know. DependencyReportMetadata's request page has the same policy. Note the reported instances sit on Controls[0], the template's own control, not on a derived one. VERDICT: the runner is legitimately less here. What would invalidate this entry is the runner emitting the built-in controls itself -- a decision to stop relying on the template, not a defect. The entry is falsifiable on the measured build either way: it is not versionContingent, so it reds the run if it ever stops matching.

Measured the same way as XmlPort.Controls.ControlGUID's entry, which carries the full statement of the probe and its 12-of-37 discrimination. OUT OF SCOPE as well as unobservable, under the repository owner's standing translations decision of 2026-09-10 relayed on #3568 -- the same call the seven TranslationKey entries in allowlist.json record, reaching the xmlport request page because #4467 made that subtree measurable. WriteXmlPortRequestPageXml's own doc comment already names these attributes as deliberately not written and says it is a scope decision, NOT a claim they are underivable: the key is COMPUTED from names rather than stored and 2,153 of 2,153 reproduce (TranslationKeysAreDerivable_NotAPermanentLimit). What invalidates this entry is the owner putting translations back in scope.
